rationale: All four lenses and the standards audit ran with parseable output, nothing was truncated, no standards coverage gap was reported and the diff was not oversized; every deduped candidate was verified against source inside budget, 22 of 26 were dismissed as false positives, spec-approved design decisions or below the emission floor, and nothing was deferred, so no deferred backlog file was written. Blocking: the acceptance timer and the retention entry both survive an untrack and are silently overwritten on re-track (src/hooks/useAuthCallbackListener.ts:211,239), producing false and duplicated 'timeout' beacons, purging a retry's retention mid-window and leaving a timer that outlives unmount - the audited one-beacon-per-id constraint and AC 1 on the retry path both fail. One decision_needed remains: chat's rollback predicate silently drops a late IdP error that the sibling consumer applies (src/store/chatGeneration.ts:301), which the approved spec mandated but AC 3 and consumer parity contradict, so confidence is low.

findings.title: Acceptance window derived twice; helper unused in production
findings.problem: The effect computes the acceptance window inline as Math.max(resolvedHintMs, AUTH_CALLBACK_ACCEPTANCE_MS) at :181, while the exported getAuthCallbackAcceptanceMs() at :117 expresses the same rule against the runtime config. Grepping the whole of src/ shows the helper's only callers are useAuthCallbackListener.test.tsx:531 and :537 - the two tests that certify AC 2's '600 s by default' and 'widens, never clamps' behaviour. No production path executes it, and the two expressions are not interchangeable: the effect honours the timeoutMs option, the helper does not.
findings.impact: AC 2's derivation is verified only against a parallel implementation the app never runs, so a future edit to either side leaves the tested rule and the executed rule disagreeing with a green suite - the exact drift the acceptance window exists to prevent. It also leaves a dead exported symbol on the module's public surface (alongside AUTH_CALLBACK_HINT_MS, which likewise has no consumer).
findings.recommendation: Make the effect call the helper - e.g. const resolvedAcceptanceMs = timeoutMs ? Math.max(timeoutMs, AUTH_CALLBACK_ACCEPTANCE_MS) : getAuthCallbackAcceptanceMs() - so the tested function is the executed one, or delete the helper and assert the acceptance deadline through the rendered hook instead. Drop AUTH_CALLBACK_HINT_MS from the export list if nothing consumes it.

findings.title: Acceptance timer and retention survive untrack and re-track
findings.problem: The untrack branch at :211-227 clears only hintTimeoutsRef; acceptanceTimeoutsRef[id] stays armed and retainedIdsRef still holds the id. The tracking branch at :239 then assigns a fresh acceptance handle over the stale map entry without clearing it. Two live consequences follow. (a) An id untracked before its hint fires - cancel, clearRows, chat switch, a row replaced - keeps a 600 s timer that runs onIdAcceptanceExpiry (:201-209) and POSTs result:'timeout' for a flow nobody was awaiting; before this change untracking cleared the only timer. (b) On the retry path (hint expiry rolls the row back and untracks it, the user clicks again and the id is re-tracked) the orphaned first timer fires at its original deadline, deletes the map entry that now holds the retry's handle, runs retainedIdsRef.delete(id) while the retry's own window is still open, and beacons; the retry's handle is by then unreachable, so the unmount cleanup at :352-364 cannot clear it and it beacons again later, from a page the user has left. Retention also survives a chat switch, so useChatAuthCallbacks (:50-51, handlers bound to currentChat.id) routes a late success at whichever chat is open rather than the originating one.
findings.impact: Breaks the constraint this change was required to hold - exactly one beacon per id at acceptance expiry - in both directions: duplicate beacons for a retried id and false 'timeout' records for cancelled or abandoned flows, corrupting the EPMCDME-14226 metric the move to acceptance expiry exists to protect. It also reintroduces the ticket's own defect on the retry path: the second attempt's retention is purged early, so the late callback is dropped as untracked (AC 1). The spec's Retention rule - untracking for any reason other than a hint expiry purges tracking and retention together - is not implemented.
findings.recommendation: In the untrack branch clear acceptanceTimeoutsRef[id] and delete it from the map alongside the hint handle, and remove the id from retainedIdsRef, so untracking for any reason other than a hint expiry tears both stages down. Additionally clearTimeout any existing acceptance handle before arming a new one at :239 so a re-track can never orphan a timer. Cover both paths in useAuthCallbackListener.test.tsx with navigator.sendBeacon stubbed: (1) untrack an id before its hint fires, advance past the acceptance deadline, assert no beacon; (2) untrack after a hint expiry, re-track the same id, advance past the first attempt's deadline and assert the retry's retention still accepts a success and that exactly one beacon is sent for the id; (3) unmount with a flow pending, advance 600 s, assert no beacon.

findings.title: AC 6 retry pin missing for the chat consumer
findings.problem: AC 6 requires a regression test that retrying after a hint expiry re-runs initiate() and does not reuse a consumed PKCE state, naming both consumer sites. The pin exists only in useMCPAuthPrompt.test.tsx. chatGeneration.promptAuth.test.ts covers markPromptAuthSuccess/rollbackPromptAuthRow only, and the pre-existing initiate/continue cases in chatGeneration.test.ts never involve a hint expiry, so nothing asserts that a chat row rolled back by onTimeout leaves no stale pending_initiate for continuePromptAuth to reopen.
findings.impact: The chat path's retry behaviour after a hint expiry is unasserted, which is the one path this change makes newly reachable (the row can now be rolled back and later receive a callback). A regression that reopened a consumed auth_url would ship green.
findings.recommendation: Add a case to chatGeneration.promptAuth.test.ts that rolls a row back via rollbackPromptAuthRow with the hint message, then drives the retry through initiatePromptAuth/continuePromptAuth and asserts a fresh initiate is issued and pending_initiate is not reused. If the implementers concluded this case cannot be driven RED because no production change was expected, record that verdict in the test file rather than leaving the criterion uncovered.

findings.title: Late IdP error never reaches the chat row
findings.problem: isAuthSuccessTarget was widened to row.status !== 'authenticated' (:299) but isAuthRollbackTarget still requires row.status === 'authenticating' (:301), and rollbackPromptAuthRow (:958) uses it. After the hint expiry, onTimeout has already rolled the row to a recoverable status, so a late error callback - now deliverable because the id sits in the listener's retention set (useAuthCallbackListener.ts:294-304, 342) - finds no matching row and is silently discarded. The sibling consumer disagrees: useMCPAuthPrompt.onError (:225-233) updates by auth_config_id regardless of status, and the diff adds a test asserting exactly that ('lands an error context on the row when onError arrives after a hint expiry').
findings.impact: In chat, a sign-in the identity provider denies after 60 s leaves the row showing 'Sign-in is taking longer than usual. It can still complete - or click to try again.' indefinitely instead of the denial reason, while the same callback surfaces the reason in the assistant auth gate. Two consumers of one listener behave differently on the same event, and AC 3's 'a callback arriving after the UI stops showing the spinner is still applied' holds only for the success half.
findings.recommendation: Human decision needed: the approved spec explicitly mandates 'rollback still requires authenticating', but AC 3 and consumer parity argue the other way, and the stated goal in the comment ('never clobber an authenticated row') is met by the weaker predicate too. Either widen isAuthRollbackTarget to accept recoverable statuses (row.status === 'authenticating' || isRecoverableStatus(row.status)) and amend the spec line, or confirm the drop is deliberate, document why chat keeps the optimistic copy after a denial, and reconcile useMCPAuthPrompt's behaviour with it. Whichever is chosen, pin it in chatGeneration.promptAuth.test.ts with a rollback case on a non-'authenticating' row.
